name: Grand Hyatt Shenzhen
positioning: Grand Hyatt in a 38-storey building in Shenzhen's Luohu District, set above a metro hub and next to the MixC Shopping Mall, minutes from the Hong Kong border crossings
best_for: Travelers moving between Shenzhen and Hong Kong
Guests who want a city-center base connected to the metro and shopping
Longer stays in an apartment with a full kitchen

facts.text: Grand Hyatt Shenzhen is in the heart of the city, within its established commercial and financial district.
The hotel is housed in a distinctive 38-storey crested building.
The MixC Shopping Mall is adjacent to the hotel.
Standard rooms have a glass-enclosed marble bath with a rain shower and a separate tub.
The two-bedroom apartment has a living room, dining area, study and fully equipped kitchen.
The Chairman Suite has a dining table for 10, a full kitchen and a private massage area.
The Grand Club offers guests in Club rooms and suites breakfast, afternoon tea, evening cocktails and a selection of wines.
The heated pool is on the 3rd-floor terrace and has a sun deck.
Shui Xiang Spa offers massages, facials and body treatments.
The 24-hour fitness centre includes a foot reflexology and hydrotherapy area, a yoga studio and a steam room.
China Lodge is a Cantonese restaurant on the 35th to 37th floors with panoramic views of Shenzhen.
The Lounge on the 33rd floor looks out over the Shenzhen cityscape and the green mountains of northern Hong Kong.

highlights.text: The hotel sits directly above a major transportation hub served by five intersecting metro lines.
The hotel is just minutes from the Luohu, Futian and Liantang border crossings, giving easy access between Shenzhen and Hong Kong.
All rooms and suites have floor-to-ceiling windows with Shenzhen city views and Hong Kong mountain views.
The Show Kitchen on the 32nd floor has floor-to-ceiling windows with views of both Shenzhen and Hong Kong.

considerations.text: The hotel recommends that international guests use local mapping apps such as Gaode Map or Baidu Map, as international mapping apps may not be accurate in Chinese Mainland.
Guests must wear a swimming cap in the pool, per Shenzhen Health Bureau regulations.
WhataHotel notes that this large-scale hotel may feel less intimate for some guests.
